facts.statement: Mochlodon is a genus of rhabdodontid dinosaurs found in Austria and Hungary.
facts.quote: Mochlodon is a genus of rhabdodontid dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of Austria and Hungary.

facts.statement: The genus name Mochlodon refers to a bar-like ridge on the teeth, derived from Greek words for 'bar' and 'tooth'.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek mokhlos, "bar", and odon, "tooth", a reference to the bar-like median ridge on the teeth.

facts.statement: Fossils of Mochlodon were first reported in 1859 from the Gute Hoffnung mine in Austria.
facts.quote: In 1859 coal mine administrator Pawlowitsch notified the University of Vienna that some fossils had been found in the Gute Hoffnung mine at Muthmannsdorf in Austria.

facts.statement: Emanuel Bunzel originally described the type species as Iguanodon suessii in 1871.
facts.quote: Bunzel in 1871 named the euornithopod a new species of Iguanodon: Iguanodon suessii.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley established the separate genus Mochlodon in 1881.
facts.quote: In 1881 Harry Govier Seeley named a separate genus: Mochlodon.

facts.statement: The type specimen dates to the Lower Campanian, approximately 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: The type specimen PIUW 2349 was found in the Grünbach Formation of the Gosau Group dating from the Lower Campanian, about 80 million years old.

facts.statement: The dentary bone was designated as the lectotype for Mochlodon in 2005.
facts.quote: In 2005 the dentary was chosen as the lectotype.

facts.statement: A second species, Mochlodon vorosi, was described from Hungary in 2012.
facts.quote: A second species, M. vorosi, was described from the Santonian aged Csehbánya Formation of Hungary in 2012.

facts.statement: A 2026 study concluded that Mochlodon vorosi is a junior synonym of the ceratopsian Ajkaceratops.
facts.quote: In 2026, Maidment and colleagues reassessed this species in the context of new cranial remains of the coeval Ajkaceratops, and concluded that the M. vorosi material represented the same taxon as Ajkaceratops.

facts.statement: A 2005 study suggested the Austrian remains might belong to Zalmoxes because no unique features were found for Mochlodon.
facts.quote: In 2005 a study concluded that no unique derived features, autapomorphies, could be established for Mochlodon in relation to Zalmoxes, assigning the Austrian remains provisionally to a Zalmoxes sp.

facts.statement: Mochlodon is classified within the family Rhabdodontidae.
Mochlodon lived between 85 and 80 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, entre 85 a 80 millones de años desde el Santoniense al Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Mochlodon spans from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Maastrichtian (85.7 to 66 million years ago)
